Sampled 'outswam' hits are swim-meet reports, not statements of the form. Every model holds 'swim - swam' and the out- pattern (outran, outshone), so it most likely builds 'outswam' from them. Rated likely, not very likely: Wikipedia's irregular-verb list and Wiktionary do state it.

A verb that forms its past tense like an.why: Treated as definitional, like the template's 'a building observes the time zone of its city': saying a verb inflects like another with a prefix just means its past is the prefix plus the other's past. So this premise never gives way; what can give way is whether this particular verb inflects like its base (the second premise).
